topics.title: 课程作业与教师要求
topics.summary: 学生有责任明确每门课程教师的具体要求；各项考核的AI许可因课程而异，在规则不明确时学生须先向任课教师咨询核实。
topics.scope: 各课程教学大纲与单项作业具体要求
topics.evidenceScope: Individual course syllabi and assignment instructions

claims.text: Office of Student Conduct guidance establishes that students are responsible for knowing instructor expectations regarding AI tools for courses and assignments.

evidence.quote: Students are responsible for knowing their instructor’s expectations when it comes to using AI tools.
evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence (Office of Student Conduct and Community Standards)

topics.title: 考场纪律与测试规范
topics.summary: 如果不清楚某课程或作业是否允许使用AI，学生有责任在使用前询问教师。
topics.scope: 课程考核与考场纪律规范

claims.text: When it is unclear whether AI is allowed in a course or assignment, students are responsible for asking the instructor before use.

evidence.quote: If it is unclear whether AI tools are allowed in a particular course or for an assignment, it is the student’s responsibility to ask their instructor before using them.
evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence (Office of Student Conduct and Community Standards)

topics.title: AI披露与大纲说明
topics.summary: 学校鼓励任课教师在教学大纲中向学生明确说明AI期望；全校统一的大学图书馆强制引用标准属于未核实政策缺口。
topics.scope: 大纲教学规范（全校统一强制引注未核实）

claims.text: Instructors are guided to communicate course-specific AI expectations; mandatory university-wide citation templates remain an unverified gap.

evidence.quote: UW–Madison encourages instructors to share their expectations regarding students’ use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools both at the beginning of a course and throughout the semester.
evidence.title: AI statements for course syllabi (Center for Teaching, Learning & Mentoring)

topics.title: 数据安全与FERPA保护
topics.summary: 除非经过适当的内部审查，不得向生成式AI工具或服务输入敏感、限制级或其他受保护数据。
topics.scope: 校级数据安全分级与FERPA合规标准
topics.evidenceScope: Institutional data classification and FERPA guidance

claims.text: Sensitive, restricted or otherwise protected data must not be entered into a generative AI tool or service unless it has undergone appropriate internal review.

evidence.quote: You may not enter any sensitive, restricted or otherwise protected data into any generative AI tool or service unless it has undergone appropriate internal review
evidence.title: Generative AI at UW–Madison: Use & Policies (DoIT)
evidence.location: Prohibited Use and Relevant Policies table

topics.title: 校园企业级AI工具
topics.summary: 威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校为符合条件的教职工与学生提供微软Copilot Chat；全校统一采购多款商用平台的企业许可属于未核实政策缺口。
topics.scope: 知识库已审查企业AI工具目录

claims.text: Microsoft Copilot Chat is made available to eligible university members; multi-tool campus-wide licensing terms remain an unverified gap.

evidence.quote: Web-grounded AI chat and document Q&A, available to all users through Microsoft 365.
evidence.title: Generative AI Tools Available at UW–Madison (KnowledgeBase 154501)

topics.title: 涉人科研与IRB审批
topics.summary: 依据2026年7月22日机构审查委员会（IRB）指引，在涉及人类受试者的科研中使用AI工具必须在方案中详述并获IRB前置审批，对受试者数据及PHI适用严格分级保护。
topics.scope: 人类受试者保护计划（HRPP）IRB操作规范
topics.evidenceScope: Human Research Protection Program (HRPP) IRB guidelines

claims.text: Human Research Protection Program guidelines mandate that any AI usage in human participant research must be described in the IRB application and approved prior to use.

evidence.quote: any use of AI in a research study must be described in the IRB application and/or study protocol and receive IRB approval before implementation.
evidence.title: Using AI as a Tool (Human Research Protection Program, July 22, 2026)

additionalTopics.title: 学术诚信与不端处理
additionalTopics.summary: 学生行为规范指引建议教师在怀疑未经许可使用AI时，直接联系学生面谈沟通相关顾虑。
additionalTopics.scope: 学生行为规范与威斯康星行政法典UWS 14章
additionalTopics.evidenceScope: Student conduct guidance and Chapter UWS 14 framework

claims.text: Student conduct guidance instructs that an instructor suspecting unauthorized AI use should contact the student directly to discuss concerns.

evidence.quote: If your instructor suspects you have used ChatGPT or other AI tools contrary to their expectations, they should contact you directly to have a meeting about their concerns.
evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence (Office of Student Conduct and Community Standards)

additionalTopics.title: 教学原则与学生隐私
additionalTopics.summary: 卓越教与学中心（CTLM）教学原则指导教师设计有教育意义的评估、保护学生知识产权与FERPA记录，并在学期中持续明确考核规则。
additionalTopics.scope: 卓越教与学中心（CTLM）教学指导原则
additionalTopics.evidenceScope: Center for Teaching, Learning & Mentoring (CTLM) guiding principles

claims.text: CTLM guiding principles establish educator responsibilities for protecting student privacy, intellectual work, and securing FERPA-protected records.

evidence.quote: Instructors and administrators are responsible for protecting student privacy and intellectual work, as well as securing FERPA-protected data. They must also follow university policies that apply to the use of generative AI.
evidence.title: Guiding Principles for Generative AI in Teaching (CTLM)
evidence.location: Protect Data and Intellectual Property section

additionalTopics.title: IT安全与代码审查
additionalTopics.summary: 学校指引要求在实施前对AI辅助生成的代码进行人工监督与审查；针对所有商用AI工具的正式集中采购审批流程属于未核实缺口。

coursework.en: Students are responsible for knowing each instructor's specific expectations; permissions vary across courses and assignments, and students must ask their instructor if guidelines are unclear.

exams.en: When it is unclear whether AI is allowed in a course or assignment, students are responsible for asking the instructor before use.

disclosure.en: Instructors are encouraged to communicate specific syllabus AI expectations to students; standardized university library citation mandates for all courses remain an unverified gap.

privacy_data.en: Sensitive, restricted or otherwise protected data must not be entered into a generative AI tool or service unless it has undergone appropriate internal review.

approved_tools.en: UW–Madison provides Microsoft Copilot Chat to eligible students and staff with institutional credentials; campus-wide enterprise licensing for multiple commercial platforms remains an unverified gap.

research_publication.en: Under the July 22, 2026 IRB guidance, any use of AI tools in research involving human participants must be detailed in the IRB protocol and approved prior to implementation, with strict data classification applied to participant data and PHI.

academic_integrity.en: Student conduct guidance provides that an instructor suspecting unauthorized AI use should contact the student directly to have a meeting regarding their concerns.

teaching_guidance.en: CTLM guiding principles direct educators to design pedagogically meaningful assessments, protect student intellectual property and FERPA records, and continuously articulate course expectations.

security_procurement.en: Institutional guidance requires human oversight and review of any AI-assisted code before implementation; formal centralized procurement approval workflows for all commercial AI tools remain an unverified gap.
security_procurement.zh: 学校指引要求在实施前对AI辅助生成的代码进行人工监督与审查；针对所有商用AI工具的正式集中采购审批流程属于未核实缺口。

claim-uwmadison-001.text: UW-Madison publishes an official generative AI use and policies page that says faculty, staff, students, and affiliates must follow UW-Madison, UW System Administration, and Board of Regents policies when using generative AI tools and services.

evidence.quote: All university faculty, staff, students and affiliates must follow these policies. As with everything you do at the university, you must follow UW-Madison, UW System Administration (UWSA) and UW System Board of Regents policies when using generative AI tools and services.

claim-uwmadison-002.text: UW-Madison states that sensitive, restricted, or otherwise protected data may not be entered into a generative AI tool or service unless the tool has undergone appropriate internal review.

evidence.quote: You may not enter any sensitive, restricted or otherwise protected data into any generative AI tool or service unless it has undergone appropriate internal review.
evidence.location: Section: Prohibited use and relevant policies

claim-uwmadison-003.text: UW-Madison identifies use of AI-generated code in institutional IT systems or services without human review for malicious elements as a prohibited use.

evidence.quote: Using AI-generated code for institutional IT systems or services without review by a human to verify the absence of malicious elements
evidence.location: Section: Uses of generative AI explicitly prohibited by policy

claim-uwmadison-004.text: UW-Madison's CTLM generative AI teaching guidance says instructors and administrators are responsible for protecting student privacy and intellectual work, securing FERPA-protected data, and following university policies that apply to generative AI.

evidence.quote: Instructors and administrators are responsible for protecting student privacy and intellectual work, as well as securing FERPA-protected data. They must also follow university policies that apply to the use of generative AI.
evidence.location: Section: Protect Data and Intellectual Property

claim-uwmadison-005.text: UW-Madison Student Conduct guidance says students are responsible for knowing their instructor's expectations for AI tools and should ask before using AI if permission is unclear.

evidence.quote: Students are responsible for knowing their instructor's expectations when it comes to using AI tools. If it is unclear whether AI tools are allowed in a particular course or for an assignment, it is the student's responsibility to ask their instructor before using them.

claim-uwmadison-006.text: UW-Madison Registrar guidance says UW-Madison-provided AI meeting summarization tools are generally approved for use with FERPA data, but unit leadership decides whether and how they may be used.

evidence.quote: UW-Madison-provided AI meeting summarization tools are generally approved for use with FERPA data. Unit leadership decides whether the tools may be used, including restrictions on the types of meetings it can be used for.

claim-uwmadison-007.text: UW-Madison states that it has vetted and secured contracts for listed generative AI services that are available university-wide for free and provide higher data security and privacy protection than public services.

evidence.quote: UW-Madison has vetted and secured contracts for the generative AI services below. These tools are available university-wide for free and provide higher data security and privacy protection than public services.
evidence.location: Section: Access generative AI tools at UW-Madison

claim-uwmadison-008.text: UW-Madison CTLM encourages instructors to communicate expectations for students' use of generative AI tools early and throughout a course, including through syllabi, Canvas, and course discussion.

evidence.quote: UW-Madison encourages instructors to share their expectations regarding students' use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools both at the beginning of a course and throughout the semester. Instructors may communicate their expectations to students in a variety of ways such as via their syllabi, in Canvas, and during course discussions and activities.
